questions.prompt: The savage monster, which the whole race feared, destroyed the temple.
questions.answer: Mōnstrum saevum, quod omnis gēns timēbat, aedem absūmpsit.

questions.prompt: With a broken oar the sailor struggled against the fierce sea.
questions.answer: Frāctō rēmō nauta contrā mare ferum luctābātur.

questions.prompt: The impious king, drunk with wine, scorned the gods' warning.
questions.answer: Rēx impius, vīnō ēbrius, deōrum admonitiōnem sprēvit.

questions.prompt: We saw the lofty houses of the city from the top of the hill.
questions.answer: Altās aedēs urbis ex summō colle vīdimus.

questions.prompt: The greedy master, tenacious of his gold, guarded the doors by night.
questions.answer: Dominus avārus, aurī tenāx, iānuās noctū custōdiēbat.

questions.prompt: The lover praised the maiden's beauty with generous words.
questions.answer: Amātor virginis fōrmam līberālibus verbīs laudāvit.

questions.prompt: On the fifth day the faithful hand of the soldiers seized the citadel.
questions.answer: Quīntō diē fīda mīlitum manus arcem cēpit.

questions.prompt: The idle young men, given to drunkenness, wasted their fathers' riches.
questions.answer: Iuvenēs dēsidiōsī, ēbrietātī dēditī, patrum dīvitiās absūmpsērunt.

questions.prompt: The spicy food pleased the guests at the long banquet.
questions.answer: Cibus piperātus convīvīs in longō convīviō placuit.

questions.prompt: Led on by hope, the general led his forces across the river.
questions.answer: Spē adductus, dux cōpiās trāns flūmen dūxit.

questions.prompt: The savage race of the mountains used to worship a cruel monster.
questions.answer: Fera montium gēns crūdēle mōnstrum colēbat.

questions.prompt: Your temple, destroyed by fire, will be restored by our hands.
questions.answer: Aedis vestra, igne dēlēta, manibus nostrīs restituētur.

questions.prompt: The guardian of the gate watched the citizens with tenacious eyes.
questions.answer: Portae custōs cīvēs oculīs tenācibus servābat.

questions.prompt: Overcome by idleness, the attendants neglected their duty.
questions.answer: Dēsidiā victī, ministrī officium neglēxērunt.

questions.prompt: The leader, tenacious of victory, feared no danger.
questions.answer: Dux, victōriae tenāx, nūllum perīculum timēbat.

questions.prompt: The generous citizen gave gifts to the people on the festival day.
questions.answer: Cīvis līberālis populō diē fēstō dōna dedit.

questions.prompt: Terrified by the monster's fierceness, the boys fled through the fields.
questions.answer: Mōnstrī feritāte territī, puerī per agrōs fūgērunt.

questions.prompt: The old man, drunk and idle, wasted many days in sleep.
questions.answer: Senex, ēbrius et dēsidiōsus, multōs diēs somnō absūmpsit.

questions.prompt: The impious deeds of the race displeased the gods.
questions.answer: Impia gentis facta deīs displicuērunt.

questions.prompt: On the fifth day the fleet returned to the harbor with broken oars.
questions.answer: Quīntō diē classis frāctīs rēmīs in portum rediit.

questions.prompt: The woman entrusted her hope to the faith of the gods.
questions.answer: Fēmina spem suam deōrum fideī crēdidit.

questions.prompt: The enemies destroyed the citadel with savage fury.
questions.answer: Hostēs arcem ferā rabiē absūmpsērunt.

questions.prompt: The leader's warning pleased the soldiers in the camp.
questions.answer: Ducis admonitiō mīlitibus in castrīs placuit.
